links.outcome: Comparison of LLM-generated versus physician-authored ED one-liner summaries on accuracy, completeness, utility
links.effect: LLM summaries rated higher: accuracy 4.18 vs 3.40 (β=0.78, p<.001); completeness 3.69 vs 3.25 (p=.005); utility 3.88 vs 3.21 (p<.001). LLM preferred in 50.5% of encounters, physician in 38.4%.
links.quote: Across all dimensions, LLM-generated summaries received higher ratings than physician-authored summaries.

unlisted_practices: Using k-nearest-neighbor few-shot prompting to generate LLM summaries from multi-encounter clinical notes
Analyzing LLM note-selection behavior and how inclusion of specific note types affects summary quality

screen.reason: The study is an offline retrospective evaluation comparing LLM-generated vs physician-generated clinical one-liner summaries rated by emergency physicians. It does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
